hero: In the water treatment room of a Philippine freestanding dialysis unit in Batangas, a Filipina resident physician, a dialysis charge nurse and a water treatment technician stand beside blue carbon tanks and a reverse osmosis unit, the technician holding a chlorine test strip against a color chart while the physician reads the logbook; fluorescent light, pipes and gauges, serious and cooperative mood, no text.

figures.teaches: Dialysis water is treated in stages, and the carbon tanks are the barrier against chlorine and chloramine, tested after each tank to catch breakthrough.
figures.content: Left-to-right flow diagram on white. 'Source water (municipal, well or tanker)' -> 'Sediment filter (particles)' -> 'Softener (calcium, magnesium)' -> 'Carbon tank 1' -> test point icon 'Total chlorine test' -> 'Carbon tank 2' -> test point icon 'Total chlorine test' -> 'Reverse osmosis (most dissolved salts, metals, bacteria, endotoxin)' -> 'Distribution loop' -> three dialysis machine icons. Under the carbon tanks: 'Remove chlorine and chloramine'. Callout box 'AAMI limits: chloramines 0.10 mg/L; free chlorine 0.50 mg/L'. Second callout 'ISO/AAMI water: bacteria <100 CFU/mL (action 50); endotoxin <0.25 EU/mL (action 0.125)'. Warning flag at tank 1 test point: 'Breakthrough here = only one barrier left: test tank 2, tell the medical director'. Small side note 'Tanker water, pipe repair, flood or brownout: test before every shift'. '© renalcarematters.com' bottom right.

figures.teaches: A cluster response follows a fixed order: protect patients, alert, keep evidence, check the water, list cases, then report and fix.
figures.content: Six numbered tiles in two rows. 1 'Protect patients now: treat, culture before antibiotics, stop sessions on the suspected supply'. 2 'Tell: charge nurse, technician, medical director, attending, infection control'. 3 'Keep the evidence: dialyzers, tubing, lot numbers; sample water and dialysate before any change'. 4 'Check the water: chlorine before and after each carbon tank, RO readings, source changes, disinfection dates'. 5 'Line list: chair, machine, shift, access type, onset time, temperature, cultures'. 6 'Report and fix: DOH and facility rules; restart only with medical director sign-off'. Header strip: 'Two or more patients unwell on one shift = cluster until proven otherwise'. '© renalcarematters.com' bottom right.

card: Blue carbon tanks and a reverse osmosis unit in a dialysis water treatment room, a chlorine test strip and color chart resting on a logbook, no people, no text.
